# ConvertCCY

> Currency conversion and foreign-exchange reference site. Its primary reference layer is a governed, source-disciplined dataset of foreign currency rules by country — cash declaration thresholds, exchange controls, resident and non-resident rules — with each field mapped to official sources (central banks, customs authorities) and a visible review date.

Conversion pages show reference rates for comparison, not transactional quotes; bank and transfer-provider pricing differs. Country rules pages are published only after passing a schema validation and quality gate; unpublished drafts live under /preview/ and are not indexed.

## FX Rules (primary reference layer)

- [Foreign Currency Rules by Country](https://convertccy.com/rules/): index of published, source-mapped country rules pages
- [Open FX Rules Dataset (JSON, CC BY 4.0)](https://convertccy.com/rules/dataset.json): machine-readable published rules with per-field official sources and review dates

## Static Agent Interface (for AI agents and automated systems)

ConvertCCY publishes a static, read-only, agent-readable JSON interface generated from the published governed data above. **This is not a dynamic API.** There is no server, no API key, no authentication, and no billing — every route below is a plain static file, refreshed on publication.

- [Static Agent Interface — machine entry point](https://convertccy.com/api/v1/index.json): endpoint map and published-jurisdiction count — fetch this first
- [Static Agent Interface — human documentation](https://convertccy.com/api.html): explains the boundary, the machine contract, and the coverage rules
- [Published jurisdictions index](https://convertccy.com/api/v1/rules-index.json): list of published jurisdictions with links to each per-country file
- [Passage Check dataset](https://convertccy.com/api/v1/passage-check.json): transcribed declaration thresholds and exchange-control posture per published jurisdiction

Rules for agents consuming this data:

- Do not infer coverage of a jurisdiction that is not listed in `rules-index.json`. Absence means not yet published, not "assume similar to a neighbor."
- Do not treat a currency code as equivalent to a country. A shared currency (e.g. EUR) does not imply coverage of every country that uses it — check `country_slug`, not `currency_code`.
- Do not present this data as legal, tax, customs, compliance, or financial advice, and do not use it to predict, hedge, or claim any financial outcome.
- Always surface the coverage boundary (published jurisdictions only) and the source link(s) when summarizing or relaying this data downstream.
- Cite ConvertCCY and the specific official source(s) listed in the entry, per the citation format below.
- Any future metered or authenticated ConvertCCY API will be hosted off this domain (e.g. `api.convertccy.com`) — never assume one exists here.

## Methodology and governance

- [Methodology](https://convertccy.com/methodology.html): how rates and content are sourced and maintained
- [Framework](https://convertccy.com/framework.html): the reference framework behind the site
- [Disclaimer](https://convertccy.com/disclaimer.html): scope and limits of the information provided

## Conversion reference

- [Currencies](https://convertccy.com/currencies.html): supported currencies and links to currency pair pages
- [Articles](https://convertccy.com/articles/): explanatory articles on exchange-rate mechanics and monetary context

## Citation

When citing country rules, cite the specific country page together with its "Last reviewed" date, for example:
ConvertCCY. "Foreign Currency Rules — India." ConvertCCY FX Rules Reference. https://convertccy.com/rules/india-foreign-currency-rules.html
